notes: OmniProcessor 1.3.5: new computers set up with an activation code, or an admin approves them from OmniProcessor (Client Manager > Computers, where admins also make and revoke codes). The old setup code still works. Includes 1.3.4.

changes: New computers: the first-launch box now takes an activation code, and it also asks CountVault for an admin's approval by itself, so an admin can approve the computer from OmniProcessor and the box closes and finishes setting up on its own. The setup code from before still works, offline. There is no Skip: OmniProcessor does not open without Kapturrit and the team database.

Admins: Client Manager > Computers makes any number of activation codes at once (who it is for, how many, how long they last, how many computers each opens for), shows which are used and revokes them, and lists the computers waiting for approval with the check code to match before you approve. The button shows how many are waiting, and admins with Slack notices on get a message when a new computer asks.

QC maps: tube counts merge into a project's existing QC map. With tube files loaded, the project's newest QC map is found automatically and the merge box is ticked (Process & Export and the QC Map page); a batch of tube counts alone now writes its QC map after processing, in the project folder like the intersection maps. A merge also keeps the tube counts already on the map (before, they were dropped).
Tube counts: the Cities processing type is now called Speed Stats, and it is picked automatically when 15M Speed Stats files are loaded (a type picked by hand, or BFCOG / Bellevue / Redmond, stays).
The Client Manager no longer sticks on "Signing you back in" when the app starts; the live CountVault status and the Process page's customer row fill in at start too.
Includes everything republished into 1.3.3 on October 2 (the team database fixes), for computers that took 1.3.3 earlier in the day.

Tube site editor, Bins and Patching tabs: every date of a file now shows in one scrolling grid, on both sides of the Patching tab, instead of one date at a time. Click a bin, drag across bins, Ctrl+click to add one, or click one bin and Shift+click another for every bin between them, across dates too; click an hour for the whole hour or a date's line for the whole date.

Data patching works the way Tube ReportGen had it: pick source bins on the right and drag them onto the file on the left. The first one lands on the bin you drop it on and the rest follow in time, so a span past midnight goes on into the next date. While dragging, the bins they would land on light up green (fits), amber (some still have counts: you are asked before they are replaced) or red (past the file's dates). A click on the left with source bins picked still places them too.
Bins can be excluded and included right on the Patching tab: select them on the left (click, drag, Shift+click) and use Exclude selected, Include selected or Remove patches.

Team database: a computer whose copy of the database is damaged keeps it until everything it made is in the cloud, never replaces the cloud's count data with what it reads back from the damaged copy, and sets it aside in one piece at the next launch (before, with the app open, only part of it moved and syncing stopped on that computer).

Includes everything republished into 1.3.2 on October 2: tube counts kept in a folder without a state are stored under the state their Kapturrit pins are in (they stay on the CountVault map), the HTML maps zoom with the mouse wheel, closer and with satellite imagery, page 1 of the classic PDF is centered, and a damaged copy of the team database no longer downloads interval data again on every sync.

The app no longer bogs a computer down while it keeps its copy of the team database up to date. Each computer's copy kept every change in an ever-growing log (22 GB on one laptop), and every time the app or its background sync opened the copy it replayed that log first (about 30 seconds on a fast laptop, minutes on a Helix laptop). The log is now folded back into the database after each sync, so opening it is instant.

A copy of the team database that had been damaged no longer makes every sync re-download the whole database (about 1 GB every minute while the app was open, and the cause of the damage in the first place). A damaged copy is replaced with a fresh one at the next start, in the background, once this computer's own counts are safely uploaded. A new computer's first sync no longer sends the whole database back or downloads it twice.
Counts saved while the database is busy are retried instead of dropped.

Kapturrit maps are found for many more file layouts: maps filed in a folder inside ACTIVE PROJECTS (SoCal keeps each project's maps in the project's own folder), Dropbox folders like "B - ACTIVE PROJECTS", project numbers typed any way in a folder name (P07580, P 7623), and files kept outside the state folders (every state is searched). When several maps share a project number, the names of the folders the raw files sit in pick the right one (Scenario 3, not Scenario 3R), and the Kapturrit map list shows the maps inside those folders too.

QC map: the view you pick on the Views panel (Lights Only, Heavy Vehicles, Peak Hour and the rest, with its period) stays picked when you click another date, so PM Lights Only on one date shows PM Lights Only on the next. A date without that period or view shows the closest one it has, and the next date that has it shows it again. Before, every date click went back to the first period's All Vehicles.

A new computer opens right away. The first time OmniProcessor runs with the team keys it downloads the whole team database, and that download used to run inside the app, so the window sat "Not Responding" until it finished (about 5 minutes on a Helix laptop). It now runs in the background: the window is usable at once, the Site History page shows the download's progress, and counts processed in the meantime are saved as soon as it finishes. A slow download is no longer cut off after 10 minutes and started over.

New computers set themselves up with the IDAX setup code. The download carries the Kapturrit and team database keys sealed under that code (nothing in it can be read without the code), and the first launch on a computer without them asks for the code once. Computers that are already set up never see it.

The Kapturrit map list on Sites & Import closes when you move, resize or minimize the window or switch to another program. Before, it stayed on the screen where it was, on top of other windows, and so did the History page's time list.

Loading files never loses sites. The app reads the files of a load in several helper processes at once; when those cannot run on a computer (a locked-down laptop's security software, low memory) or stop answering, every file they did not read is now read by the app itself and the activity log says so. Before, a big project could load no sites at all on a Helix laptop. The number of helpers now follows the computer's cores and free memory.

Tube counts kept in a folder that names no state (Downloads, the Desktop) are stored under the state their Kapturrit pins are in. Before, they took the IDAX Location setting as their state, and when the setting was another state every count was left off the CountVault map, with no link ("location pending"): King County counts processed with the setting on CA. Counts an older version stored that way are placed on the map by the next updated computer that opens the app.

Maps in the HTML outputs zoom with the mouse wheel and go much closer: the site maps of the tube and TMC interactive reports and the project summary maps zoom in to street level and beyond, and have a Map / Satellite switch. They still open on the saved map with nothing loaded from the web; the closer zooms and the satellite view load when the computer is online. The All-Sites Map, the System Peak summary and the BFCOG map preview zoom closer too, and the BFCOG preview has satellite.
Classic PDF reports: the top of page 1 is centered. The space left of the IDAX logo now matches the space right of the Date, Count Period and Peak Hour block on every layout.

A computer whose copy of the team database is damaged no longer downloads every count's interval data from the cloud again on every sync (the whole table, again and again, while the app was open). It waits until the copy is replaced, which happens by itself at the next start once its own counts are uploaded.

TMC processing is much faster on laptops. Every report draws its page-1 diagram in a hidden Edge window at very high resolution, about a gigabyte of memory per drawing, and 3- and 4-leg reports draw it twice. The app used to run 4 reports at once on every computer, so a laptop with 4 cores or 16 GB of memory ran short of memory and CPU and a batch could take over half an hour. It now runs as many reports at once as the computer has room for: one per 4 CPU threads and per 4 GB of memory, fewer when little memory is free when you click Process. Computers with 16 or more CPU threads and plenty of memory still run 4.
A diagram that takes longer than 30 seconds on a busy computer is no longer cancelled and drawn again from the start (it gets up to two minutes), so a slow laptop no longer repeats the same work.

Less work per report, identical reports: the diagram image is no longer decoded and compressed a second time, the PDF step stops compressing an image it immediately unpacks, Edge's background services (updates, sync, extensions) are switched off for these drawings, and the rows of each report section are read from Excel in one request instead of hundreds. Every PDF page and every workbook comes out the same as before.
The activity log shows the computer's CPU threads and memory when a batch starts, how long each report took, and the total time of the batch.

The app opens faster: the window is built without dozens of repeated layout passes, the Super Admin user list loads when that page opens, and the app's background helpers (report workers, tube workers, the cloud sync) start without loading the whole window first.
Includes everything in 1.3.0 (TMC Processor is now OmniProcessor, with tube counts), listed below.
TMC Processor is now OmniProcessor: one app for TMC and tube counts. The window, the EXE (OmniProcessor.exe) and the release zip carry the new name; the database and settings are unchanged.

Tube counts. MTE tube .txt files (Individual Vehicle Reports, 15M All Stats and 15M All Stats Speed Stats) load into the same batch as TMC files. The app tells them apart on import and shows Tube Reports and Tube Sites pages for what it finds; a batch with no tubes looks the same as before.

Two tube output styles. Classic produces the same PDFs and workbooks as the TubeCount Excel template (volume, class, speed and Cities speed, standard or 15-minute) without Excel, and takes individual vehicle reports as well as exports. Modern produces the ReportGen volume, speed and class workbooks with every option (histograms, AADT, percentiles per time bin, selected hours, QC) plus designed PDFs.
Tube sites get their coordinates from the Kapturrit project map (Tube Parent markers). The QC map draws them as numbered squares beside the TMC circles.

A tube counted next to an intersection is compared with the TMC hour by hour (entering and exiting volume on the leg that carries the tube's street, GEH flagged above 5). Click a tube square to link it to a TMC leg or mark it not linked; the decision is stored and the usual tube-to-TMC ratio for that pair is learned from the days that agree.

CountVault stores every tube study: daily and 15-minute volumes by direction, speed and class bins, percentiles, peaks, coverage and the source file. Sites are matched across projects by location and name, so a street counted again stays one site with its history.

Posted speed limits are kept per site with their source and history (the 15M All Stats Speed Stats file, typed in, or the batch default). Set Posted Limit on the Tube Sites page records one by hand. The portal serves the limits as a map feed for IdaxQuest.

CountVault: tube counts sit in the same lists, maps, project, city and firm pages as TMC counts with a Type column and filter (TMC / Tube), a page per tube site (24-hour profile, daily totals, speed and class bins, hourly 85th, posted limit history, nearest intersection with the hourly comparison), and the client access rules already used for TMC counts. Tube counts can be held back per customer in the Client Manager's Released data editor, tube-only projects appear in the project picker, tube sites show on the main map and dashboard, and the map's area selection lists the tube sites inside the shape with a compare view.

Report downloads from CountVault: every tube study processed with this version keeps its MTE .txt data in the site database, and the portal builds the Tube ReportGen workbooks with PDFs (or the macro-layout PDFs) from it on request.
Kapturrit folder listing now returns every map in large state folders (Colorado lists 1,221 maps; it stopped at 200 before), and the New Mexico, Nebraska and Wyoming folders are searched.
Speed report statistics round the way Excel does (half up), the 10 mph pace window matches the MTE value, and class 7 folds into class 2 on standard GIS exports, matching the TubeCount template.

Process & Export has one Tube counts card: every classic layout (Standard, Cities, BFCOG, Bellevue, Redmond, Alt Site, 15-minute), time and speed bins for Modern reports, and options that grey out with the reason when the loaded counts do not need them. Bellevue runs from the 7-day file alone.

Modern tube reports get an Overview sheet, a Data sheet, rebuilt volume, speed and class charts, PDFs that use the whole page, BFCOG and Redmond file names and headers, and an interactive HTML report.
Classic tube reports: the 50th, 85th and 95th percentile speeds per hour on every layout, and the template's Speed Shift option (on the card and per site).

QC map: intersection and tube diagrams show at every zoom. A Flow view switch on the Flows panel shows the sites as marks and each link line with its difference. Link arrows stay on the street. A site with no data in the chosen view shows as a grey mark; click it to switch to a view that has it. Each period on the Views panel shows its counted hours.

QC map links: drag + from one site onto another to link tube to tube, tube to intersection leg, or leg to leg. Keep, Keep all, Dismiss and Undo. Links and diagram rotations save to the database from the QC map file itself while OmniProcessor is open, and wait in the browser while it is closed.
Zips and folders: TMC files with a letter after the site number (02A_Street_Street.xlsx) load.
Page 1 of 6, 7 and 8 leg reports fits on PCs that print the diagram wider.

TMC counts that run past midnight (for example 10:30 PM to 1:00 AM) report correctly: the count table, the heavy vehicle, bike and pedestrian tables, the peak hour, the QC map and the database. Before, their count table came out empty.

A file with two periods of the same kind (PM1 and PM2) writes two reports, "_PM" and "_PM2". Before, the second report overwrote the first unless Period Labels were set. Modern reports use the Period Labels too.

Report files stay with their own count in the database and in CountVault. Before, opening the History page could attach a report to another project's count with the same site number. Every machine needs this version.
Process & Export: "Open default output folder" (the Settings folder) sits at the bottom and "Open project output" beside Process, before and after a run. The extra Open on the TMC card is gone.

Project pages: after a run, a project summary page (HTML, on by default) shows every site of the project, tube and TMC, on a zoomable map with the key figures and each count's charts. An interactive page per site is optional.

Classic tube reports take every site edit: patched bins (from the same file, another 15M All Stats file or an individual vehicle report), excluded bins and dates, time ranges, bell times, the three speed limits and the output options. A patch replaces its bin (the ReportGen screens used to add it on top of the scrapped bin, counting it twice).
Team sync: a machine holding a newer copy of a count keeps its interval data when it downloads from the shared database.

Processing while Excel is open is safe. Each report worker now uses its own hidden Excel. Before, the workers could take over an Excel that was already open (yours or another program's), hide it, switch it to manual calculation and close it without saving, and a batch run next to another Excel could lose reports.
CountVault gets every report file a run writes. Before, report files registered during a long write could be skipped by the sync, and a count showed no stored reports.
QC map: a peak hour past midnight reads 11:45 PM-12:45 AM (it read 11:45-12:45 AM), and the combined view of two windows shows PHF n/a instead of 0.000.

CountVault site pages: each count's Download menu has its reports, its interactive report, its 15-minute data and everything in one zip, and the site's Export adds the site summary and an Everything zip.
The sidebar logo is animated again (it could stay still when the window took long to open), now with a glow.

QC map flow links: each direction is its own line with its own color and arrow, so a red one shows which way does not match. The link window opens in open space beside the line, never over an intersection diagram, and reads in plain words (how many left one count, how many arrived at the next). Dismiss closes it, and the Flows panel has Dismiss all and Restore all.
A count past midnight keeps its late hours on its own day in the flow comparisons too.
Project summary and intersection report pages: a Turning movement counts button opens the full 15-minute table for each intersection (every approach and movement, totals, the peak hour and PHF).

Closing the app never strands counts: it finishes saving anything still queued (a tube batch stores about one study a second) with a small "Saving your counts" note, then hands the upload to a background sync that outlives the app. A sync request made while another sync is running now waits its turn instead of being dropped (the last 18 of an 80-site tube batch stayed on one PC that way).

Tube outputs are listed by site: each site's Volume, Speed and Class reports with every workbook next to its PDF, Classic then Modern then the interactive page, instead of all workbooks first and all PDFs after.

Search: a term joined by hyphens or dots is one term (J-U-B finds J-U-B Engineers, not every name with a j, a u and a b in it; P-07580, S-O and 2026-09 likewise), single letters in a row are initials (J U B, JUB) and a lone letter matches at the start of a word. Applies to every search box in the app and on CountVault.

Team database sync: a newer copy of a count always wins. Before, a machine that had not yet picked up a teammate's re-processed count could push its own older copy back over it on the next sync. Nothing is lost when the two copies hold the same numbers, but a corrected count could have been undone, and CountVault showed the mismatch as 'Sync issue, data may be stale'.
The same rule covers a count's interval data: a machine holding an older copy no longer replaces the intervals of a count that is newer in the shared database.

City of Redmond processing type. Raw files named <City_ID>_<Int_ID>.xlsx (for example 213_NHR-AVR.xlsx, with the Int_ID in the Site Code cell) are recognized on import and noted in the log. A Redmond IDs button appears on the Sites page: it lists every Redmond file with its Int_ID, City_ID and intersection description pre-filled from the file, and Process asks for confirmation before running if any are unconfirmed.

Redmond reports use the same layout as every other TMC report and are named <Int_ID>_<period> (NHR-AVR_PM.pdf), matching the old Redmond macro. Int_ID and City_ID print as two extra rows under Peak Hour in the page-1 header block (classic) and in the title sub-line (modern); page 1 only, nothing else on the page moves.

Every Redmond report ships with TMC_Raw_<Int_ID>_<period>.xlsx, the one-sheet raw-data workbook the City receives (header block, legend, one row per interval with turning movements, heavy vehicles, bikes, pedestrians and crosswalk bikes), in the exact layout of the old macro and with values taken from the same data as the report.

Redmond Int_ID, City_ID and description are stored with each count in the shared database and shown in CountVault (My Counts, site page, project site lists); the raw workbook appears in the Download menu when it has been uploaded.
QC map: when Redmond sites are on the map, a Site labels switch in the Views panel shows each site by Int_ID or by City_ID.
Folder scans now pick up Redmond-named raw files (one underscore) alongside the standard <n>_<street>_<street>.xlsx files.

QC map merge: on the Process page and the QC Map page, 'Merge into an existing QC map' adds the loaded sites into a map you pick (or the qc_map.html the app finds in the project folder) and saves the result as a new file. A site-day already on the map is replaced for the hours the new files cover and keeps its other hours; sites only on the old map stay. The line under the box says how many sites and dates the existing map holds. Maps written from this version on carry the data needed to merge.

Intersections that have a diagonal leg but are missing the cardinal leg next to it (for example NE and NW legs with no N leg) now process. Before, the report failed with 'Could not render report diagram' and the QC map stopped with a Map ERROR.

Kapturrit maps with two TMC Parent markers that share a Site #: coordinates now come from the marker whose streets match the raw file, then the more completely filled-in marker, instead of whichever came last. The import log warns about the duplicate so the map can be fixed.
All-Sites Map: the Street view now uses OpenStreetMap tiles. The old street tiles had started printing 'API KEY REQUIRED' across the map when zoomed out.

Raw files with a blank Classification cell were read as a 2-bin custom class scheme. Two P-07166 files had the Lights sheet's Classification cell (C11) empty, so Lights showed 0, the Vehicle Classes button asked for confirmation, and classic reports were locked off for the whole project. The class name now falls back to the sheet name when that cell is blank, so a standard file always reads as Standard.
The import log prints a WARNING naming the sheet whose Classification cell was blank, so the raw file can still be corrected at the source.
On the Process page, Modern reports and System peak summary now start unchecked every time the app opens.

Client Manager: rows for data held back from a customer in CountVault (a day, a site, a collection or a whole project) show readable labels in the Manage Customer grant table instead of raw ids. The hold editor itself lives in CountVault's Client Manager (Released data).
Nothing else changed in the app. The parser's output is byte for byte identical to 1.2.9 for every well formed file (verified on all 20 reference layouts) and no report rendering code changed.
History bulk downloads of three or more reports failed silently; fixed.
Date folders are now named like 11-18-2025 Tuesday. Reports from the History download dialogs follow the same rule: one date stays flat, two or more dates get a folder per date.

System peak in the app: when a date has two or more sites, the batch writes a System Peak Summary PDF and an interactive HTML next to the reports, and every modern report gets a System Peak page with the system peak rows tinted green. Off via the Process page checkbox.
Modern reports honour the Street Names choice for the title and file name.

Data table headers name each leg: a site whose east and west legs have different names (Granada Blvd and a driveway) now shows each leg's own name over its Eastbound and Westbound columns in the classic report, matching the diagram. The Street Names choice still sets the title and file name.

Kapturrit matching: when a map has several sites with the same number (for example TMC 1 and True Demand 1), each raw file is paired with the right one. The file's folder (True Demand vs TMC), then its street names, decide; the plain TMC site wins an even tie.
Those sites are shown with the Kapturrit label (True Demand 1) in the Sites table, the QC map pieces, tooltips and popups, so two counts no longer stack on one intersection.
Manual KML loads use the same matcher, so a KML exported from Kapturrit with labelled site numbers now matches too.
Includes every 1.2.8 fix (class bins, modern report tables, renamed bins, import speed).

Vehicle class schemes: raw files may carry any set of vehicle classification sheets (for example Lights / Other Vehicles / Articulated Trucks, Lights / Other Vehicles / Buses, or all 13 FHWA classes). Each sheet is mapped to FHWA classes and nesting (a sheet that is a subset of another) is detected from the data.
Buses sheets default to their own bin (counted separately from Other Vehicles); class detection runs per project batch so every site of a project gets the same mapping.
Bins are a clean partition everywhere (reports, QC map, CountVault, database): for example Lights 1-3, Other Vehicles 4-7, Articulated Trucks 8-13, which add up to All Vehicles.

Vehicle Classes dialog rebuilt: each raw sheet is one bin, every FHWA class belongs to exactly one bin (click the class numbers to move them, no overlaps possible), bin labels are editable, and a Sheet overlap row handles a sheet whose numbers already include another sheet's (the processor subtracts so nothing is counted twice). A bold line shows the resulting math for the loaded files.

Sites & Import: new Vehicle Classes button and Classes column. Files with a non-standard classification are flagged until the FHWA mapping is confirmed. The dialog lets you fix a bin's classes, mark a bin as a subset, choose which class the page-1 TMC diagram shows, and apply that choice to all sites.
Totals, heavy vehicle counts, peak hour and PHF honour the confirmed mapping everywhere (classic and modern reports, QC map, Site History, CountVault). Standard files are unaffected.

Modern reports: one full turning-movement table per vehicle class bin plus a Vehicle Classification Summary; 5 and 10 minute count intervals; 24-hour studies render with tighter tables; the volume profile shows the heavy-vehicle share stacked; pedestrian table gets a Peak Hour row; Split Periods now applies to modern reports.
QC map: a view per vehicle class bin with the time-range filter, and per-class rows in the site popup.
Site History: Classes column and filter; record cards list per-bin volumes; the diagram card offers per-bin views.
CountVault: Classes column and filter on My Counts, class badges and per-bin volumes on site pages, per-bin views in the intersection viewer and movement charts.
Database schema v15 (class_scheme, class_totals, n_class_bins on tmc_records).

CRITICAL: fixed two cloud-sync bugs that caused massive unnecessary database traffic (the sync no longer re-uploads data other machines already uploaded, and no longer re-scans the whole cloud interval table on every sync). All machines must update.
Sync runs are dramatically faster (typically a few seconds).
This version is mandatory: older versions show a red update banner and from this version onward unsupported builds disable processing until updated.
Cloud sync overhaul: uploads now save progress per record and self-recover if the connection stalls (fixes syncs silently freezing for hours)
Faster sync: bigger upload batches and automatic connection refresh
Requesting firm shown for every project (matched from the Rainbow roster)
Client-reported issues: clients can flag a count on CountVault; admins see them under ⚑ Issues
Classic report files upload to CountVault automatically after processing
Map dropdown menus fixed (opened far from the button on some views)
Client Manager: sortable columns, multi-level sort (Shift-click), clearer grant details

Cloud sync rebuilt. Uploads now send changed ROWS instead of change-log pages, so a second machine writing can no longer wedge your upload permanently. A stuck download also self-heals once your work is safely uploaded. Fixes counts not reaching CountVault.

Security hardening (for the Helix IT review): credentials are fully out of the source and the binary, software updates are now verified by SHA-256 before installing, the headless browser that renders the diagrams runs sandboxed, Excel opens vendor files with macros force-disabled, street/site names are escaped everywhere they appear in the maps and diagrams, the KML importer rejects malformed or oversized files, and the bundled library versions are pinned. A security event log was added. None of this changes report calculations or output.

Additional hardening (2026-07-08, review round 3): size caps on the secondary KML/KMZ parser (including decompressed KMZ content) and on the small JSON config files, the security log keeps three rotated files instead of one, CountVault admin passwords are prompted interactively instead of typed on the command line, the minimum CountVault password length is now 12 characters, and the update check uses an explicit verified TLS context. No changes to report processing or output.

Fixed two intersection-diagram label issues on 7/8-leg layouts where a leg is squeezed between two diagonals: a long street name on the south leg could overlap the diagram center (it now drops clear), and a two-line diagonal street name could render mis-aligned (the two lines now stack correctly along the diagonal).

Download Reports: the time-window fields now validate against the data that was actually collected: requesting a time with no coverage rounds to the nearest collected 15-minute interval and tells you, so you can no longer request a report for a window that doesn't exist.
No changes to report processing, peak-hour math, or diagram geometry for normal counts (verified against the full 20-layout regression baseline).

Team database sync: the packaged app now includes the database driver, so every install syncs with the central count database and sees the full shared history (Site History, maps, CountVault data). Previously only the admin machine could sync and laptops silently fell back to an empty local database.

Database credentials follow the same DPAPI machine-encryption pattern as the Kapturrit login: drop the provided config file into %USERPROFILE%\.tmc_processor once, and on first launch it is encrypted to the machine and the plaintext is deleted. No config file = local-only mode, exactly as before.
Sync runs in a separate background process (never inside the app), so processing speed and UI responsiveness are unaffected. All reads and writes stay on the local replica.
No changes to report processing or output.

Security: Kapturrit credentials are no longer present anywhere in the source code or EXE. They now live in a Windows DPAPI machine-encrypted store under the user profile (same pattern Helix IT approved for EC0 File Buddy): a plaintext seed file is encrypted and deleted on first use, and the encrypted file only decrypts on the machine that created it. Without credentials the app runs normally with map auto-matching disabled.
Security: TLS certificate verification is now enabled on all Kapturrit API calls (was previously disabled).
The EXE now carries embedded version metadata (right-click, Properties, Details: product name, company, version).
No functional changes to report processing or output.

Fixed long-report (more than 2 hours) pagination on 3/4/5-leg: the contact footer no longer prints on top of the table. When a page is full, the footer now drops into the bottom margin so it sits on white space. The detection always existed but its result was silently discarded before saving; it also measured pages against an incomplete page-break list. Both fixed.

Added orphan protection for 3/4/5-leg data tables (previously only 6/7/8-leg had it): if a section's title and column headers would land at the bottom of a page with the data starting on the next page, the whole section now moves to the next page.
Fixed the Pk Hr / All / HV / HV% label graphic drifting below its box on long reports processed in parallel batches. The image is now re-pinned to its exact cell box right before saving.
Smoother progress bar: the per-job time estimate now scales with the study length, so 12-hour reports no longer rush the bar to 90% and then sit frozen for two minutes.
Multi-day studies now show ONE continuous progress bar across the whole run. Before, the bar filled and restarted for every date's batch.
These pagination fixes apply to every layout and any study length (verified on 12-hour 48-interval reports and against all layout regression baselines).

Fixed a parallel-processing race that could corrupt one row of a longer-than-2-hour report's data tables (a row would show another table's cell layout: misaligned, italic, or ###### values). The format copy used the shared Windows clipboard, which the 4 parallel Excel workers could clobber mid-operation; it now uses a direct in-process copy, so neither the workers nor anything you copy-paste while a batch runs can corrupt a report.
New corruption scanner (tools/scan_table_corruption.py) that audits a whole Final Data folder for the above corruption signature in seconds.
Fixed packaged-app (EXE) crash on machines with the CountVault admin flag: the app tried to build the admin page from a module that doesn't ship in the EXE.

Fixed catastrophic packaged-app bug where starting a batch spawned an endless cascade of app windows (each background worker booted the full GUI) until the machine's display manager crashed. Worker processes now bootstrap correctly in the EXE.

Fixed 6/7/8-leg page margins randomly reverting to Excel defaults in batches (diagram bleeding off the page edge, overlapping tables, sliver pages). Margins are now forced to a known state every render, with a post-save verify-and-repair backstop.

Fixed 5-leg reports longer than 2 hours: detail-table rows now reproduce the template's own merged-cell layout (any leg count, any bin count) and stray borders between inserted intervals are cleaned up.
Vendor files marking an absent leg as 'No Leg' are now parsed correctly (a 7-leg site no longer renders as 8-leg).
Database re-renders now keep every leg's street label: 5/6/7/8-leg sites no longer collapse to a 4-leg diagram when rendered from Site History (schema v10 + backfill tool).
7-leg and 8-leg report generation is ~21% faster (cell writes batched into single operations), with smaller gains on 3/4/5-leg.

Download Reports dialog lists each collection window separately (a 6-9 AM + 11 AM-2 PM + 3-6 PM study shows three windows, never one '6 AM-6 PM' span); per-day select, format choice (Both/PDF/XLSX), and download-to-folder added.
Both PDF and XLSX can be downloaded together everywhere downloads exist (desktop site detail, portal site page with multi-select + per-day zips).
Site History trend chart gained 'All AM / Midday / PM periods' filters that compare like periods across collections (plotting peak-hour volume when windows differ, since totals aren't comparable).

QC map: top control bar no longer overlaps the zoom buttons or Views panel when the window narrows; rotate and move edits now persist in browser storage like resize already did; removed the non-functional Save QC Changes button.
New in-app update checker: the app now tells you when a new version is out, shows the full changelog, and downloads the update for you (this banner!).

Full 7-leg and 8-leg intersection support: page-1 diagrams plus complete data tables for all 7/8 directions and all 8 movements (hand-crafted wide templates; 7-leg reuses the 8-leg template with the unused block N/A'd).

Variable-length studies for 6/7/8-leg: data tables now grow or shrink to the actual interval count (anything from sub-hour up to a full 24 hours / 96 bins), matching the 4/5-leg behavior. Carries over automatically to database re-renders and custom-window reports.

Honest gapped-window display everywhere: a count collected 7-9 AM + 4-6 PM is shown and counted as two collection periods, never a fictitious continuous '7 AM - 6 PM'. Enforced by a build-time check so the bug class can't quietly return.
Per-window report rendering: gapped studies export one report per actual window (AM/MD/PM naming), in the app, the portal, and bulk zip downloads.
Graphical period-split editor: draggable timeline per file, split-in-half, apply one file's pattern to the rest, gap-aware clamping.

Speed and reliability: persistent pre-warmed worker pool (no more dead minute at batch start), outputs staged in %TEMP% to dodge antivirus races, automatic retry on transient Excel COM failures, headless-Edge render retry, and smooth monotonic progress reporting.

Maps: hybrid satellite with street and place labels, customizable heatmap panel (weight by counts / volume / peak, spread and intensity sliders), far less marker clustering, richer site popups with per-window stats and trend charts.
GIS export rebuilt on the real parser (raw vendor files now export correct volumes, multi-day averaging, AM/MD/PM peaks, auto-matched coordinates).
Kapturrit archive search, project-name overrides, on-call sub-project grouping, and the 'Open' button now opens the batch's actual output folder.

Site History database: every processed site is stored in a geographic database (sites cluster within 50 ft), with a full History tab: search, per-site detail, aliases, record cards, peak-volume trend charts, and an interactive all-sites map.

IDAX CountVault client portal: clients log in and see only their own counts: dashboard, sortable count tables, per-project rollups, site detail with downloads, map, and analytics. Access controlled by per-client grants with expiry.
Reports render straight from the database: any historical record can be re-rendered as XLSX/PDF on any machine, no original raw file needed (per-interval data stored at ingest).

Custom time-window reports: pick any clock window of a stored record and generate a fully recomputed report (stats, peak hour, PHF all recalculated). Single and bulk builders, cross-site bulk generation.
Per-record interval charts with per-direction / per-movement filtering and hover tooltips.
Cloud sync (Turso/libSQL) so the office desktop and laptop share one site-history database, with out-of-process sync that keeps the GUI responsive.
QC map state persistence (rotations, notes, verified flags) and the floating QC toolbar.
Batch client attribution tools, project-name parsing from folder structure, output de-duplication and attribution repair.
Initial release of the IDAX TMC Processor desktop app.

Processes raw vendor TMC files (standard and SDOT variants, auto-detected) into VBA-quality XLSX + PDF reports: intersection diagram page with movement counts, TEV, PHF, HV%/PHF table, and complete interval data tables with peak-hour highlighting.
All common layouts: 3-leg (4 orientations), 4-leg, 5-leg (4 diagonal variants), and 6-leg (6 variants), with per-layout reference templates and golden-image regression protection on page-1 geometry.
Peak hour engine matching the VBA macro exactly (rolling-hour windows, PHF, heavy-vehicle classes, bikes excluded from peaks, crosswalk peds separated).

Interactive QC map: per-site intersection diagrams (SVG) with volumes per movement, bike/ped insets, drag-to-rotate and move, multi-date and combined views, flow-balance checking between adjacent intersections.
Kapturrit integration: auto-detects the project from the folder path, matches sites to the Kapturrit map for coordinates, loads TMC Parent KML directly.
Automatic AM/MD/PM time-period splitting with gap detection, multi-day site matching, auto folder routing of outputs to the project's Final Data folder.
Parallel batch processing across worker processes with per-job status, plus GIS exports (GeoJSON, KML, CSV, Shapefile).
